political_system.executive: President of the United States is Head of State, Head of Government, and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces; holds vast executive authority subject to congressional appropriations and constitutional checks; elected indirectly via the 538-member Electoral College for a 4-year term.
political_system.legislature: Bicameral United States Congress: Senate (100 members, two per state elected for 6-year terms; confirms judicial and executive nominations, ratifies treaties) and House of Representatives (435 members apportioned by population elected every 2 years; originates revenue bills).
political_system.judiciary: Independent federal judiciary headed by the 9-member Supreme Court of the United States; holds life tenure and ultimate authority of constitutional judicial review.
political_system.structure: Federal union of 50 sovereign states, one federal district (Washington, D.C.), and 5 major inhabited territories (Puerto Rico, Guam, US Virgin Islands, Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa).
political_system.election_system: State-administered elections; predominantly single-member plurality (first-past-the-post) with primary elections selecting party nominees; electoral college system determines executive presidency.

current_government.president: Donald J. Trump (47th President of the United States)
current_government.ruling_coalition: Republican Party (GOP) controlling executive presidency and working legislative majorities in Congress following the November 2024 general election
current_government.context: Second non-consecutive administration centered on an 'America First' policy agenda, emphasizing tariff-driven trade protectionism, aggressive southern border enforcement, domestic industrial reshoring, deregulation of domestic energy extraction, and transactional re-evaluation of overseas security alliances.
current_government.main_opposition: Democratic Party, led by congressional leadership

major_parties.name: Republican Party (GOP)
major_parties.ideology: American populism, conservative nationalism, protectionist tariffs, domestic fossil fuel energy dominance, skepticism of multilateral climate agreements, strong military deterrence

major_parties.name: Democratic Party
major_parties.ideology: Modern liberalism, progressive social welfare, multilateral treaty alliances (NATO, climate pacts), clean energy subsidies (IRA), defense of democratic institutions

political_movements_and_dynamics.name: Transactional Alliance Burden-Sharing
political_movements_and_dynamics.description: Intense executive focus on demanding that NATO allies, Japan, and South Korea meet or exceed 2-3% of GDP defense spending benchmarks, threatening reduction of US military presence for non-compliant partners.
political_movements_and_dynamics.current_relevance: Drives unprecedented defense budget increases across European NATO members and accelerates allied sovereign defense procurement.

political_movements_and_dynamics.name: Aggressive Tariff Protectionism
political_movements_and_dynamics.description: Deployment of across-the-board universal baseline tariffs (10-20%) on foreign imports and targeted 60%+ tariffs on Chinese manufacturing to force industrial reshoring and reduce the trade deficit.
political_movements_and_dynamics.current_relevance: Restructures international supply chains, strains traditional trade relations with allies, and fuels international trade retaliation.

political_movements_and_dynamics.name: Fiscal Debt & Legislative Impasse
political_movements_and_dynamics.description: Rising mandatory entitlement spending and debt interest servicing costs approaching $1 trillion annually, driving persistent statutory debt ceiling battles and budget brinkmanship in Congress.
political_movements_and_dynamics.current_relevance: Creates uncertainty regarding long-term defense appropriation ceilings and foreign security assistance packages.
